findings.explanation: The module call passes key_ring_id = google_kms_key_ring.key_ring.id but the only key ring resource in the example is google_kms_key_ring.secret (defined in google_kms_key_ring.tf). Terraform would fail immediately on plan with 'Reference to undeclared resource'. No deterministic rule checks cross-resource reference consistency.
findings.remediation: Change the module call to: key_ring_id = google_kms_key_ring.secret.id
findings.title: Example module call references non-existent key ring resource google_kms_key_ring.key_ring — terraform plan fails

findings.explanation: customer_managed_encryption.kms_key_name requires a fully-qualified resource name (projects/PROJECT/locations/LOCATION/keyRings/KEYRING/cryptoKeys/KEYNAME). The config passes google_kms_crypto_key.secrets.name which returns only the short key name (e.g. 'crypto-key-abc123s'). The API will reject this with an invalid argument error, causing the apply to fail or the secret to be created without CMEK. HLD_GCP_124 only checks that the attribute is not_null, not that it is a valid full resource path.
findings.title: Secret Manager CMEK uses .name instead of .id for kms_key_name — CMEK silently fails at apply

findings.explanation: Two attribute errors compose to break the Pub/Sub topic CMEK chain. First, google_kms_crypto_key.pubsub sets key_ring = google_kms_key_ring.secret.name — the key_ring attribute requires the full resource ID (projects/.../keyRings/...) not just the short name 'key-ring'. Second, google_pubsub_topic.secret sets kms_key_name = google_kms_crypto_key.pubsub.name which has the same problem: .name returns the short key name, not the fully-qualified path. Both errors cause GCP API failures at apply time.
findings.remediation: In google_kms_crypto_key.tf line 3: key_ring = google_kms_key_ring.secret.id. In google_pubsub_topic.tf line 3: kms_key_name = google_kms_crypto_key.pubsub.id
findings.title: Example Pub/Sub KMS key uses .name not .id for both key_ring and kms_key_name — CMEK on topic fails at apply

findings.explanation: Per GCP documentation, Secret Manager only publishes rotation notifications to Pub/Sub when both rotation_period and next_rotation_time are set. With only rotation_period configured, the rotation schedule has no start anchor: the API accepts the config but never emits a rotation event. HLD_GCP_123 checks that rotation.rotation_period is not_null and therefore passes, but the rotation is effectively disabled because notifications never fire — any rotation automation listening on the Pub/Sub topic will never trigger.
findings.remediation: Add next_rotation_time to the rotation block as a variable: rotation { rotation_period = var.rotation_period; next_rotation_time = var.next_rotation_time }. Add a corresponding variable with an RFC3339 timestamp and expose it from the module. In the example, set next_rotation_time to a concrete near-future timestamp.
findings.title: rotation block sets rotation_period but omits next_rotation_time — Secret Manager never publishes rotation notifications

suggested_policies.rationale: HLD_GCP_123 checks that rotation.rotation_period is present on google_secret_manager_secret, confirming the rotation interval is configured. However, GCP Secret Manager only publishes rotation notifications — and therefore triggers any automation — when next_rotation_time is also set. A secret with rotation_period but no next_rotation_time appears compliant to the deterministic engine but never actually rotates. Adding a companion policy for next_rotation_time closes this gap and ensures the rotation schedule is fully anchored.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_005
name: Secret Manager secrets must have a rotation next_rotation_time configured
principle: governance
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  Google Secret Manager only publishes rotation notifications to Pub/Sub when
  both rotation_period and next_rotation_time are set. A secret configured with
  only rotation_period appears compliant but never emits a rotation event,
  meaning any rotation automation listening on the configured topic will never
  be triggered. A concrete next_rotation_time anchors the schedule and ensures
  the rotation mechanism is actually active.
remediation: |
  Add next_rotation_time to the rotation block:
  ```hcl
  resource "google_secret_manager_secret" "example" {
    rotation {
      rotation_period    = "7776000s"
      next_rotation_time = "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
  }
  ```
resources:
  google_secret_manager_secret:
    path: rotation.next_rotation_time
    not_null: true
